rows.solution: Rewrite the integrand so that one substitution clears it. Dividing numerator and denominator by \(\sin^2 x\) gives \(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos x} = \frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2 x}{\cot x}\), so the integral is \(\int \frac{\sqrt{\cot x}}{\cot x}\,\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\,dx\). Now put \(\cot x = t\), so that \(-\operatorname{cosec}^2 x\,dx = dt\). The integral becomes \(-\int \frac{\sqrt{t}}{t}\,dt = -\int t^{-1/2}\,dt = -2\sqrt{t} + C\). Restoring \(t = \cot x\), the answer is \(-2\sqrt{\cot x} + C\). Differentiating it back returns \(\frac{\operatorname{cosec}^2 x}{\sqrt{\cot x}}\), which is the original integrand.

Instead of partial fractions, pull \(x^2\) out of the bracket so a single substitution works: \(\int \frac{dx}{x(x^2 + 4)} = \int \frac{dx}{x^3\left(1 + \frac{4}{x^2}\right)}\). Put \(1 + \frac{4}{x^2} = t\), so \(-\frac{8}{x^3}\,dx = dt\), that is \(\frac{dx}{x^3} = -\frac{dt}{8}\). The integral becomes \(-\frac{1}{8}\int \frac{dt}{t} = -\frac{1}{8}\log|t| + C\), so the answer is \(-\frac{1}{8}\log\left|1 + \frac{4}{x^2}\right| + C\). This is the same as the partial-fraction form, since \(-\frac{1}{8}\log\left|\frac{x^2 + 4}{x^2}\right| = \frac{1}{8}\log\left|\frac{x^2}{x^2 + 4}\right|\).

rows.stem: Solve the following differential equation : \( (1 + e^{y/x}) \, dy + e^{y/x} \left( 1 - \frac{y}{x} \right) dx = 0 \)
rows.solution: Solve for the derivative first: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{-e^{y/x}\left(1 - \frac{y}{x}\right)}{1 + e^{y/x}} = \frac{e^{y/x}\left(\frac{y}{x} - 1\right)}{1 + e^{y/x}}\). The right-hand side involves \(x\) and \(y\) only through \(\frac{y}{x}\), so the equation is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), giving \(\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x\frac{dv}{dx}\), so \(v + x\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{e^v(v - 1)}{1 + e^v}\). Hence \(x\frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{e^v(v - 1) - v(1 + e^v)}{1 + e^v} = \frac{ve^v - e^v - v - ve^v}{1 + e^v} = \frac{-(e^v + v)}{1 + e^v}\). Separating the variables, \(\frac{e^v + 1}{e^v + v}\,dv = -\frac{dx}{x}\). The numerator on the left is exactly the derivative of its denominator, so integrating gives \(\log|e^v + v| = -\log|x| + \log C\), that is \(e^v + v = \frac{C}{x}\). Restoring \(v = \frac{y}{x}\), \(e^{y/x} + \frac{y}{x} = \frac{C}{x}\), and multiplying through by \(x\) gives the general solution \(x\,e^{y/x} + y = C\).

rows.stem: If \( \vec{a} \) and \( \vec{b} \) are two vectors such that \( \vec{a} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k} \) and \( \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 3\hat{k} \), then find the vector \( \vec{c} \), given that \( \vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{b} \) and \( \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 4 \).
rows.solution: Let \(\vec{c} = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}\). The scalar condition \(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 4\) gives \(x - y + z = 4\). For the vector condition, \(\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ x & y & z \end{vmatrix} = -(y + z)\hat{i} - (z - x)\hat{j} + (y + x)\hat{k}\). Equating this to \(\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}\) and comparing components gives \(y + z = -2\), \(z - x = 1\) and \(y + x = -3\). These three are not independent — adding the last two reproduces the first — so the cross-product condition alone leaves a whole line of possible vectors, and the dot-product condition is what pins \(\vec{c}\) down. From \(z = x + 1\) and \(y = -3 - x\), substituting into \(x - y + z = 4\) gives \(x + (3 + x) + (x + 1) = 4\), so \(3x = 0\) and \(x = 0\); then \(y = -3\) and \(z = 1\). Hence \(\vec{c} = -3\hat{j} + \hat{k}\). Both conditions check out: \(\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} - 3\hat{k} = \vec{b}\), and \(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 0 + 3 + 1 = 4\).

rows.subtopic: Equation of a Line in Space
rows.stem: Find the coordinates of the point where the line through \( (5, 1, 6) \) and \( (3, 4, 1) \) crosses the zx-plane.
rows.solution: A direction vector of the line is the difference of the two given points: \((3 - 5,\ 4 - 1,\ 1 - 6) = (-2,\ 3,\ -5)\). Taking \((5, 1, 6)\) as the base point, the line is \(\frac{x - 5}{-2} = \frac{y - 1}{3} = \frac{z - 6}{-5}\). Setting each ratio equal to \(\lambda\), a general point on it is \((-2\lambda + 5,\ 3\lambda + 1,\ -5\lambda + 6)\). The \(zx\)-plane is the plane \(y = 0\), so the crossing point satisfies \(3\lambda + 1 = 0\), giving \(\lambda = -\frac{1}{3}\). Substituting, \(x = -2\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) + 5 = \frac{2}{3} + 5 = \frac{17}{3}\) and \(z = -5\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) + 6 = \frac{5}{3} + 6 = \frac{23}{3}\). The line therefore crosses the \(zx\)-plane at \(\left(\frac{17}{3},\ 0,\ \frac{23}{3}\right)\).
